scope: PR-gate security verdict for feature/0.5.1 -> develop at PR head c807e0cd (12 commits over origin/develop). Lanes run: secrets/privacy over every added line, OWASP/injection review of the production delta, independent zero-caller verification of the K9 composition-root deletions, dependency lane, schema validity of the 3 ADR records + RELEASE.json + the 2 new bug records against the updated packaged schemas, specs/backlog doctor exit codes, three targeted test selections, and the local push-gate denylist scan over the pushed range. Diff-based, never a full-repo scan. Supersedes this session's earlier verdict at b7fd1c22, whose two LOW findings are remediated here.
verdict_reason: No blocking security or privacy finding on the reviewed diff, and both LOW findings from this session's b7fd1c22 verdict are fixed at this head with regression tests. Secrets/privacy: 1257 added lines carry zero credential-shaped assignments, zero PEM headers, zero e-mails, zero IPs, zero home-absolute paths, zero URLs, zero cloud/token shapes; the only bare 40-hex is RELEASE.json's `defined.sha`, under an allowlisted key. `dadaia ci push-gate-check` over the exact pushed range (operator denylist + baseline privacy patterns) exits 0. Dependency lane: pyproject.toml, poetry.lock, setup.cfg and .github/ untouched — no CVE surface moved. Injection: `release_new` keeps its anchored release-id validation and now refuses a symlinked release directory before minting, refuses when ANY minted artifact (SPEC/PLAN/TASKS/RELEASE.json) exists, and builds no shell string; the one new subprocess call in the test helper is a fixed argv list with no shell. K9 deletions verified independently, not taken on trust: every one of the 10 deleted symbols had zero call sites at the parent commit (only its own definition plus prose), zero residual references remain at head except three intentionally-updated docstrings, and the deletion removed two dead `git add -A` committers — a latent whole-tree staging footgun that maps directly onto the two open MEDIUM index-contamination bugs. Verified the deletion weakens no control: the FilePermissionSetter factory it removed had no production caller at develop either, and the live owner-only restriction (0o700/0o600) runs through the POSIX chmod fallback that remains. Governance/integrity: all three ADR records are `proposed` — no agent-written `accepted` — and now validate against the tightened decision-record-v1, whose new `^\d{4}$` pin I probed both ways (prose rejected, `0001` accepted, null still accepted); RELEASE.json and both new bug records validate; the consumed PR #223 verdict is deleted with no survivor. specs doctor 0 errors / 497 warnings (2 attributable, both the non-blocking SPEC-DOC-033 shape), backlog doctor clean, 141 tests passed across three selections, all measured with the reviewed code. Bug surface REDUCED on both touched components. Seven INFO items and one LOW are recorded for the fix lane; none is exploitable and none blocks the merge.

findings.message: K9 deleted two dead `git add -A` committers from the composition root — a latent whole-tree staging footgun removed, verified zero-caller
findings.detail_md:
`dadaia_workspace/container.py` at 18c6edc9 deletes `_definition_committer` and `_closure_committer`, each of which ran `["git", "-C", str(repo_root), "add", "-A"]` followed by a commit. I verified the zero-caller claim myself rather than accepting it: `git grep -w <symbol> b7fd1c22 -- dadaia_workspace tests docs` returns, for each of the ten deleted symbols, only its own definition plus prose/docstring mentions — no call site anywhere. At head the only residual references are three docstrings in `core/models/findings.py`, `features/specs/doctor.py` and `features/specs/doctor_closure_audit.py`, all intentionally rewritten by the same commit to record the deletion.

Why this matters for security: a library function that sweeps an entire working tree into a commit can fold another session's staged work — or an untracked artifact holding secrets — into history. That is exactly the hazard behind the two records still `open` (`concurrent-sessions-share-git-index-commit-boundary-contamination`, `concurrent-agent-git-add-clobbers-other-sessions-staged-files-into-unrelated-commit`, both MEDIUM) and behind proposed ADR 0002, and DADAIA §7.3 already forbids a blanket `-A`. The code was dead, so this is latent-hazard removal, not a live-vulnerability fix.

Residual (out of range, unchanged here): `infrastructure/git_subprocess.py::_stage_files_safe` is still a whole-tree-equivalent stager, but it was hardened at v0.4.3 (non-zero `git add` exit raises `GitSyncError`; every untracked path wrapped in `:(literal)` pathspec magic) and skips embedded repos.
findings.fix_recommendation: No action — recorded as positive posture evidence. When ADR 0002 is decided, cite this deletion: the library no longer ships any `git add -A` call site, which strengthens the 'practice, not library code' argument for deferring the two index bugs.

findings.message: Deleting the FilePermissionSetter factory weakens no control — the live owner-only restriction is the POSIX chmod fallback, which remains
findings.detail_md:
`_build_permission_setter()` (deleted at 18c6edc9) selected the POSIX/Windows `FilePermissionSetter` adapter that hardens the telemetry state dir and DB to 0o700/0o600 (CWE-732 surface; the protocol docstring also names the Tier-1 panel auth token).

Verified it was never a live control: `git grep -n "permission_setter=" origin/develop -- dadaia_workspace` returns nothing — production never injected it, at develop or at the parent; the only call sites are in `tests/unit/features/telemetry/test_service_chmod_guard.py`. `features/telemetry/service.py::_restrict_owner_only` documents and implements the fallback: with no injected setter it calls `os.chmod(path, mode)` directly, guarded by `PLATFORM.has_posix_chmod`. So on POSIX the restriction still happens; on Windows it is deliberately skipped as a documented, accepted Tier-2 posture that predates this range.

One factual consequence worth routing to the architect: after this deletion `FilePermissionSetter` has no production construction site at all. Proposed ADR 0001 lists it as one of the four 'real seams' with two production adapters that justify keeping a Protocol — the adapters exist, but nothing wires them.
findings.fix_recommendation: No security action. Hand the last paragraph to `software-architect` before ADR 0001 is put to the operator, so the 'four real seams' evidence is corrected or the telemetry wiring is restored intentionally.

findings.message: The tightened ADR schema is a public asset that was not re-projected — the workspace instance still carries the permissive copy
findings.detail_md:
c807e0cd edits `dadaia_workspace/public/schemas/ADRs/decision-record-v1.schema.json` (adding `"pattern": "^\\d{4}$"` to `supersedes` and `amends`) — correctly at the library source, never a hand-edited projection. But the manifest-listed projection of that asset in this workspace instance now differs: a byte compare of the repo source against `.dadaia/agentic/schemas/ADRs/decision-record-v1.schema.json` reports DRIFT, and `.dadaia/agentic/manifest.json` does list `decision-record`.

Impact is bounded: no runtime code loads this schema (the only reference is a docstring in `core/models/adr.py` saying the dataclass mirrors it, pinned by `tests/contract/test_adr_record_schema.py`, which passes). So today the drift is documentation-only rather than a validator running the stale rules. It still leaves the operator's standing rule unmet — a library change is not finished until the instance reflects it.
findings.fix_recommendation: Run `dadaia public stage && dadaia public install --target all && dadaia public doctor` from the workspace root and confirm `[ok] public-privacy`. This is an instance-side action outside the repo tree; it does not gate CI and does not need to land in this PR.

findings.message: A projected public script still names a symbol this range deleted
findings.detail_md: `dadaia_workspace/public/scripts/lint-memory-atoms.py:34` still reads `# the subprocess call site in container.py's \`_memory_lint_gate\`.` — `_memory_lint_gate` was deleted at 18c6edc9, so the comment now points at nothing. It is the one residual reference to any deleted symbol that was not updated (the three `build_findings_store` docstrings were). It matters slightly more than an ordinary stale comment because `public/` assets are projected into consumer workspaces.
findings.fix_recommendation: One-line comment fix in `public/scripts/lint-memory-atoms.py`, folded into the next commit that touches `public/` (T-051-11 K3 rewrites the projection surface). Re-project afterwards.

findings.message: The `release-new-...` bug record describes a predicate that was superseded twice inside this same branch, and the second no-clobber hole closed without a record
findings.detail_md:
`specs/bugs/BUGS.jsonl` record `release-new-refuses-a-verdicts-only-lane-directory` (written at 862881cd) states `solution: "No-clobber keyed on SPEC.md; mkdir exist_ok; ..."` and `evidence_diff: "net-neutral: predicate moved from dir to SPEC.md, ..."`. Two later commits on the same branch changed that predicate again: 231b0c55 widened it to any minted artifact (`_RELEASE_ARTIFACTS = ("SPEC.md","PLAN.md","TASKS.md","RELEASE.json")`) and c807e0cd added the symlink refusal. The record therefore no longer describes the shipped code.

231b0c55 in particular closed a real hole — at b7fd1c22, `release new <id>` would mint a fresh Draft `SPEC.md` into a directory already holding PLAN/TASKS/RELEASE.json — and it carries no ledger record of its own. Per DADAIA §7.3 every contract break found while operating the tooling is registered; a fix-to-a-fix inside the same branch is the easiest one to lose.
findings.fix_recommendation: Either update the existing record's mutable governance fields (`solution`, `evidence_diff`) to describe the final three-part predicate, or append one record for the 231b0c55 hole with `caused_by: release-new-refuses-a-verdicts-only-lane-directory`. Prefer the second — it keeps lineage visible for the next reviewer, and this predicate has now moved three times.

findings.message: Both new bug records leave `cause` null, adding 2 SPEC-DOC-033 warnings to the 495 already on develop
findings.detail_md: `release-new-refuses-a-verdicts-only-lane-directory` and `tests-tree-walkers-outside-the-ratchets-still-race-the-xdist-quarantine-probe` both set `"cause": null` while carrying a populated `root_cause`, so `dadaia specs doctor` reports `status 'resolved' is missing cause (SPEC-DOC-033, WARNING — never a block, D15)`. These are the only 2 of 497 warnings attributable to this range; the other 495 are the same shape, already on develop. The doctor exits 0.
findings.fix_recommendation: No action on this PR. Route the systemic shape to T-051-09's ledger-parser consolidation: collapse `cause`/`root_cause` into one field, or make the write seam populate both, so the 495-warning floor disappears rather than being carried forward.

findings.message: 8 pre-existing BUGS.jsonl records violate the bug-record-v1 `evidence_diff` prefix pattern (all outside this range)
findings.detail_md: All 532 ledger records validated against `public/schemas/bugs/bug-record-v1.schema.json`: 8 fail, every one already on `origin/develop` (develop carries 530 records, this range adds exactly 2, both valid). Each of the 8 carries a free-text `evidence_diff` such as `'+4 lines (skip marker)'` instead of the required `^(net-negative|net-positive|net-neutral):\s*\S.*$`. Ids: `windows-xdist-workers-crash-on-unit-fast-tier`, `ci-portability-tests-landed-without-a-gha-run-ansi-and-unit-timeout`, `push-gate-own-repo-slug-not-excluded-from-a-git-worktree-outside-repos`, `gitleaks-generic-api-key-fires-on-40-hex-git-sha-in-verdict-handoff`, `tier-ceiling-trips-under-coverage-instrumentation-on-windows-contract-coverage-job`, `contract-radon-import-undeclared-dependency-breaks-fresh-dev-install-pytest-collection`, `contract-coverage-ci-shallow-checkout-collapses-resolved-commit-derivation-to-head`, `contract-pr-verdict-check-gate-windows-runner-resolves-wsl-bash-not-git-bash`. The drift accumulated because no writer validates on append.
findings.fix_recommendation: Route to `project-manager` as ledger hygiene, not to this PR. Structural fix belongs with T-051-09: validate every record against the packaged schema at the single write seam in `features/bugs`, then correct the 8 in one governance-field sweep. Note this is the same class of gap the ADR schema just closed by adding a pattern — the schema pin only bites if something validates.

findings.message: The tests/tmp xdist race family is closed by exhaustive replacement, but no contract test forbids the next raw walker of the tests tree
findings.detail_md:
Verified at this head: `grep -rn "TESTS_ROOT.rglob\|_TESTS_DIR.rglob" tests` returns nothing (exit 1), and all four walkers now call `tests/helpers/suite_files.tracked_test_files` (`test_test_suite_ratchets.py:136,199,264`, `test_frozen_clock_aging_ratchet.py:115`, `test_harness_env_contract.py:64`, `test_no_local_helper_copies.py:51`). I swept every remaining `rglob`/`os.walk` under `tests/` for one that could still enumerate `tests/tmp/`: none can — the rest are rooted at `dadaia_workspace/`, `public/`, a `tmp_path` fixture or a narrow subtree, and `tests/conftest.py:221`'s write guard walks only `_GUARDED_DIRS = (.claude, .agents, .codex, .dadaia)`.

Residue: the guard that exists (`test_ratchet_scope_is_the_tracked_suite_never_a_tests_tmp_probe`) pins the helper's scope, not the invariant 'every scan of the suite goes through the helper'. A newly added `Path(...).rglob("*.py")` over `tests/` would pass every test and re-open the family a fourth time.
findings.fix_recommendation: Add one source-scan contract assertion — no file under `tests/` calls `rglob`/`glob`/`os.walk` on a path rooted at the tests tree outside `tests/helpers/suite_files.py` — in the existing ratchet file. One assertion, no new branch in any feature; it converts 'closed by grep today' into 'closed by construction'.

findings.message: This verdict is only valid while c807e0cd is the PR head, and the CI gate still needs it committed on the branch
findings.detail_md:
Two operational facts:

1. No `specs/releases/0.5.1/verdicts/` directory exists at this head — the consumed PR #223 verdict was correctly deleted by 9ddfa0fc, with no survivor (DADAIA §4.2 upheld). `.github/scripts/pr-verdict-check.sh` reads only a COMMITTED copy at `specs/releases/<id>/verdicts/<reviewed-sha>.handoff.json`, keyed on `agent == "security-reviewer"`, `verdict == "APPROVED"` and a 40-hex `metrics.commit_sha`. I was scoped to write nothing under the repo, so `security-verdict-gate` fails closed until this file is committed there.
2. The branch moved twice during this review: b7fd1c22 -> 231b0c55 -> c807e0cd, and my first verdict (at b7fd1c22) was invalidated in flight. That handoff has been deleted so two APPROVED verdicts never sit on disk at once. The gate's coverage rule allows only verdict-evidence paths to differ between the reviewed sha and the head, so any further production commit invalidates this verdict too.
findings.fix_recommendation: Commit this file verbatim as `specs/releases/0.5.1/verdicts/<metrics.commit_sha>.handoff.json (the full 40-hex is carried once, in metrics.commit_sha)` on `feature/0.5.1`, push, and open/refresh the PR without further code commits. If more code lands first, re-dispatch security-reviewer on the new head rather than carrying this file forward. Delete the committed verdict immediately after the merge consumes it.

decisions_required: Freeze feature/0.5.1 at c807e0cd long enough to commit this verdict and merge; any further production commit requires a re-review, as the last two did.
Whether the ledger gets a new record for the 231b0c55 no-clobber hole or an in-place correction of the existing release-new record (finding 5).
Whether FilePermissionSetter should be re-wired in production before ADR 0001 is put to the operator, since it now has adapters but no construction site (finding 2).
